Hi Anna — thanks for the clear ask. Two pragmatic options we can move on quickly:

Option A — Time extension (lowest friction)
- Extend the POC by 3 weeks (same capacity + retained KV cache).
- One-time invoice: $6,000 (covers reserved GPU window + priority engineering check-in).
- Same SLA, one additional engineering check-in during extension.
- Amendment: simple one-page addendum (DocuSign-ready).

Option B — Credit swap (procurement-friendly)
- Keep current end date but apply a one-time platform credit of $5,000 to the POC account.
- Credit can be used against token consumption or converted to a discounted first-month invoice on a committed plan.
- Includes a 60-minute onboarding call with our integration engs.

A third, higher-cost path if you need faster results:
Option C — Acceleration fee (same-day priority)
- 4-week extension with a $9,000 acceleration fee to prioritize engineering support and run an expedited model tuning cycle.
- Includes daily syncs for the first week and a guaranteed bug-fix SLA for integration blockers.

We can convert any of these to a short amendment/PO-friendly invoice. If procurement prefers a credit instead of an invoice, Option B is the cleanest. I've attached a draft amendment (POC_Extension_Amendment_Draft.docx) you can review and I can push a DocuSign link once we agree.

Next step: which option would your procurement team prefer, and do they need us to bill a purchase order number or sign the DocuSign amendment?
